chunks: And he (peace be upon him) used to say:

Make the oppressor swear, when you want his oath, that he is free from Allah's might and power, for if he swears falsely by them, punishment will be hastened for him; and if he swears by Allah, the One there is no god but He, he will not be hastened [in punishment], because he has affirmed the Unity of Allah, the Exalted.
ai.seo_question: Why does an oppressor's false oath by Allah's might bring swift punishment while an oath by Allah's name does not?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) distinguishes between general divine attributes and the specific name of God (Ism al-Jalalah) to determine the immediacy of retribution for false oaths. In Shia exegesis, swearing by 'might and power' (Hawl wa Quwwah) is considered a lesser invocation; thus, a liar is swiftly punished as a sign of divine urgency. Conversely, invoking the Unity of God (Tawhid) carries greater weight, allowing for a delay in punishment to preserve the sanctity of the Divine Name.
